newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes edge up amid quiet markets.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes edge up amid quiet markets.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes edged up with benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Tuesday, while discount levels stayed flat as refiners sorted out their supply needs for May, traders said.
Buyers were analyzing what crudes to buy following a Friday's jump in discounts for Alaska North Slope (ANS), the regional benchmark grade.
Exxon sold a 400,000 barrel cargo of ANS crude Friday at $1.32 off May WTI, a 0.27 cent widening since the last deal.
Outright prices stood at $18.53/18.73 a barrel, a 10-cent increase from Friday, in line early firmness in NYMEX crude.
Despite a heavy supply of imports for May, a leading seller of ANS priced shipments at $0.95 cents under WTI.
ARCO, normally a seller of Wilmington crude, looked to buy the grade for May as their production slipped. The grade, rarely traded on the spot market, was rpiced 75 to 85 cents over postings.
Line 63 and California heavy crude markets remained well-supplied, with no deals reported Monday or Tuesday.
